```{r}
#| label: import-data

# read all rds files for county and rbind together
dat_raw <- suppressMessages(
  ss_import_data(
    input_path = "R:/data_branches/nb_water_quality/processed_data/assembled_data", 
    county = tolower(region)
  )
)

dat <- dat_raw %>%
  qc_pivot_longer(qc_tests = c("grossrange", "depth_crosscheck")) %>%
  filter(grossrange_flag_value != 4) %>%
  qc_pivot_wider() %>%
  select(
    region, waterbody, station, lease, latitude, longitude,
    deployment_range, string_configuration,
    sensor_type, sensor_serial_number, sensor_depth_at_low_tide_m, timestamp_utc,
    any_of(vars)
    #contains("flag")
  )

# unique waterbodies
waterbodies <- sort(unique(dat$waterbody))

fig_caption <- " water quality data."
table_caption <- "Deployment details for"

i = 1 # counter for table
k = 1 # counter for figure number
text_size <- 3.5
crs <- 4326

```

# Introduction

The New Brunswick Department of Agriculture, Aquaculture, and Fisheries (DAAF) measures [essential ocean variables](https://goosocean.org/what-we-do/framework/essential-ocean-variables/) around the coast of New Brunswick through their Coastal Monitoring Program. This Program is a collaboration between DAAF, the Centre for Marine Applied Research (CMAR), Fisheries and Oceans Canada Gulf Region, and several third-party field contractors. 

This document presents deployment details and summary figures of Water Quality data collected in the **`r region`** region of the province (Figure `r k` and Figure `r k+1`). The data are available for download from the New Brunswick [Open Data Portal](https://gnb.socrata.com/browse?sortBy=alpha&page=1&pageSize=20). 

This document should be considered as a guide only, since data collection and retrieval are ongoing. The information may be revised pending ongoing data collection and analyses. 

```{r}
#| label: nb-map
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| error: false
#| fig.width: 8
#| fig.height: 5.5

# for map inset
dummy_coords <- import_map_params(tolower(region))
x_min <- min(dummy_coords$longitude)
x_max <- max(dummy_coords$longitude)
y_min <- min(dummy_coords$latitude)
y_max <- max(dummy_coords$latitude)
 
nb_bbox <- c(xmin = -68.25, xmax = -63, ymin = 44.39, ymax = 49)

sf_use_s2(FALSE) # need this to turn off spherical geometry to include QC
nb <- filter(PROV, PT == "NB"| PT == "PE"| PT == "NS"| PT == "QC") %>%
  st_crop(nb_bbox) %>% 
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

can_us <- ne_countries(
  continent = "North America", returnclass = "sf", scale = "large"
) %>% 
  st_crop(nb_bbox) %>% 
  st_transform(crs = st_crs(nb))

# box for inset map
region_box <- data.frame(
  lat = c(y_min, y_min, y_max, y_max),
  long = c(x_min, x_max, x_max, x_min)
) %>% 
  st_as_sf(coords = c("long", "lat"), crs = st_crs(can_us)) %>%
  summarise(geometry = st_combine(geometry)) %>%
  st_cast("POLYGON") 

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = can_us, linewidth = 0.5, col = "grey30") +
  geom_sf(data = region_box, col = "red", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.75) +
  theme_map() +
  coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
  theme(
    panel.border = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1),
    text = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none"
  )
```

## Data Collection 

DAAF collects temperature, pH, dissolved oxygen, and salinity data following [CMAR Coastal Monitoring Program](https://cmar.ca/coastal-monitoring-program/) procedures. Stationary moorings called "sensor strings" are deployed at a station for several months to a year. A typical sensor string consists of a rope attached to the seafloor by an anchor and suspended by a sub-surface buoy, with sensors attached at various depths (Figure `r  k`). Data are logged every 10 minutes to 1 hour, depending on the sensor and settings. Sensors must be retrieved to offload the data. The retrieval method depends on the sensor configuration, and may include triggering an acoustic release, directly removing sensors from surface moorings, or employing divers or grappling methods (Table `r i`). 

```{=typst} 
#figure(image("images/sensor_string.png"))
```
**Figure `r k`:** Example sensor string configuration (not to scale).

\newpage

After sensors have been retrieved, the offloaded data is sent to CMAR to be compiled and sent to the New Brunswick Open Data Portal for publication. CMAR also generates summary reports of the data (e.g., this document), and hosts links to the published datasets and reports on their [Data Access Map](https://cmar.ca/coastal-monitoring-program/).

## Quality Control

An automated Gross Range test was applied to the data to identify outlying and unexpected values. For consistency with the CMAR Water Quality data, each data point was assigned a flag of “Pass”, “Fail”, or “Suspect/Of Interest” [@RN25922]. 

Observations flagged as "Pass" were within the measurement range listed in the sensor specifications sheet. These observations are shown in the figures below. Observations flagged as "Fail" were outside of the measurement range and are not shown in the figures.

These automated flags were reviewed by human experts, and modified where necessary.

\newpage
# New Brunwick `r region` Water Quality Data

Water Quality data is presented by waterbody. For each waterbody, there is a table of deployment details followed by figures showing the data at each station. Note the differences in scales between figures (x-axis, y-axis, and colour).

```{r}
#| label: report-body
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| error: false
#| fig.width: 8.5
#| results: asis

for(i in seq_along(waterbodies)){

  waterbody_i <- waterbodies[i]
  dat_i <- dat %>% filter(waterbody == waterbody_i)

  stations <- sort(unique(dat_i$station))
  
  if(i > 1) cat("\n\n\\pagebreak\n")
  
  cat('\n##', waterbody_i, '\n')

  cat('\n')

  # waterbody table
  table_i <- ss_write_report_table(dat_i, keep_waterbody = FALSE) %>% 
    ss_format_report_table() %>% 
    width(width = c(2.4, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2.4, 3.8), unit = "cm") %>%
    set_table_properties(layout = "autofit") 


  i_table <- i + 1
  print(glue("\n**Table {i_table}:** {table_caption} {waterbody_i}."))
  flextable_to_rmd(table_i) 

  cat('\n')
  
  # plot for each station
  for(j in seq_along(stations)){

    k = k + 1
    station_j <- stations[j] # station of interest

    # subset data to station of interest
    dat_j <- dat_i %>% 
      filter(station == station_j) %>%
      ss_convert_depth_to_ordered_factor()
    
    # height of figure j
    h <- calc_fig_height(dat_j, h1 = 2.4)

    # figure    
    p <- ss_plot_variables(
      dat_j,
      standard_do_ylims = FALSE,
      standard_sal_ylims = FALSE,
      yaxis_newline = FALSE
    )
    
    cat('\n###', station_j, '\n')
     
    subchunkify(p, fig_height = h, fig_width = 8.5, dpi = 300)
    
    # figure caption    
    fig_caption_j <- paste0("**Figure ", k, ":** ", station_j, fig_caption)
    
    cat('\n', fig_caption_j, '\n')
    
    cat('\n')
  }
}

```
